runs.name: e9-v2-recorded-harness
runs.basis: The command tools/research/v6/e9/v2/qualification_run.py builds at the snapshot, which qualified every E9 v2 attempt: -X utf8, addopts=-q, no cacheprovider, the qualification_guard plugin (forbids entropy, NativeMatchService.run and ProcessMatchController.run), an external basetemp, plugin autoload disabled, PYTHONUTF8=1. The harness itself is not called because it writes attempt evidence.

not_reproducible_from_commits.reason: Asserts that the raw working-tree bytes of all 1,203 files pinned by v2_inherited_preservation_manifest_01.json equal their pins (except the superseded .gitattributes). 28 pins record the original research machine's Windows working tree, not committed content: 17 are CRLF renderings of the adoption-commit (2dd8f69) blobs and 11 are mixed-line-ending bytes that were never committed in that form. No checkout of any commit, on any platform, reproduces them.
not_reproducible_from_commits.evidence: 2026-10-31: in a fresh checkout of the snapshot exactly these 28 pins mismatch; the 11 mixed-EOL identities were found, read-only, only in the original research worktree D:\Projects\BATTLE2 (e.g. client/tests/test_canonical_reader.py: 74 CRLF of 76 line endings). The manifest file itself is protected by the current-tree guard and its bytes are unchanged.
not_reproducible_from_commits.disposition: Excluded from the historical run by exact node ID and reported here as a reproducibility limitation, not as a pass. run-historical instead checks at the snapshot, read-only, that the working tree mismatches the preservation manifest in exactly these working_tree_pins (with exactly these pinned values) and the superseded .gitattributes (whose bytes must equal the recorded superseding SHA-256), so the other 1,174 pins are still verified and the limitation cannot silently widen.
